utterances.text: The night after he told me that there was more to the story than he had said in the first statement, he called the witness unit and told them that it was important that he see me the next day. So I met him the next day, and he said that he was willing to tell more, give me more information in a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in each of the subsequent statements that you took from him, did he, in fact, tell you more details that he had not given you in the first statement?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't want to make a mistake. We are now talking about a third statement, and that was just some small clarifications that the team lawyers asked me for. I was thinking about the fourth statement, where he came with more information. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's do this in order, then. The first statement you took from him was after you had returned here to The Hague, or was that still in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The first statement was held in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first statement had to do basically with the general events that had happened to him in Bosanski Samac and the people that are accused in this proceeding; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the second statement deal with?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The second statement was about a phone conversation that we taped, when he called Branislav Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you briefly describe to the Court the circumstances under which that phone call was made and why that phone call was made?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: After he told me that he had to call the Defence lawyers every two weeks or 15 days, I asked, "When is the next time you are supposed to call them?" and he told me that he should have called them by now. I asked if he was willing to do a phone call and let me tape it and let me direct what to say in the phone conversation. He was willing, and I got permission from The Hague to do the taping. I told him to tell them that he was in Banja Luka because of the NATO air strike and ask them for money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then, in fact, make this phone call?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: At first, it was very difficult to get through to Serbia, but the first time we got through, he reached Igor Pantelic and he told him to call Avramovic later on. I think we tried for two days -- one or two days before we managed to get in touch with Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you then explain to the Court what happened when you finally did get in touch with Mr. Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Then the witness told him that he was in Banja Luka, asked about money. The rehearsal was discussed, I think. I'm not quite sure, but I think so. We had some problems with the tape recorder; we could see it stopped, so the interpreter was listening to the phone conversation, and afterwards, I let the interpreter translate for me what the two persons said, and then I interviewed the witness and he signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you please explain to the Court what your goal was in having him make this phone call? What did you hope to accomplish by making this phone call to Mr. Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The first call was if Avramovic didn't know him at all, we could stop the case or there was no reason to discuss it, to go any further, and if they had information about money, things like that, it could be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, continuing on to the third statement that you took from Mr. Agnes, you said that this basically was a clarification of some issues that the lawyers had asked you to put to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fourth statement that you took from him, what, in essence, did that statement focus on? What was that about?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: That was after he told me that he had some more information that he didn't want to give me because he was afraid for his relatives. As I said, he called the evening after to the witness unit and asked them to pick him up so he could meet me the next day, and then he said that he had met Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was in this fourth statement that he first told you that he had actually met Milan Simic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he explain to you why he had not told you this previously?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: He told me that he was afraid of Milan Simic and that he had a lot of power in the Samac area, and also he was afraid of the Defence lawyers. So he feared what could happen to his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, just briefly, what was the fifth statement about? What was the general subject that was in that statement?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The fifth statement -- after he signed the fourth statement, he told me he had still more, but if he gave that information, he would also make problems for non-Serbs living in Bosanski Samac, so he couldn't give it to me. Then I had several meetings with him and tried to explain how important it was that he told everything. After a while, he agreed to give us the story, but we were not allowed to write anything while he was telling the story and we were not allowed to use the information. He said that he had met Milan Simic several times in Bosanski Samac, also the Defence lawyers, he told about Mirsad Sahanic, and not so many changes in the main story, but there had been many more meetings and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you took all these statements from Mr. Agnes, how was he in dealing with the issue of dates and being specific as to when certain events occurred?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The date was all the time a problem. He didn't remember which month it was, and certainly not which day the meetings happened. We had a different definition of meetings. What I referred to as meetings was maybe not a meeting for him, so there were misunderstandings. So all the time I had to use a special criminal intelligence software, where we created time lines so he could put the meetings in the right positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also have some other meetings with Mr. Agnes since he has been here in The Hague, during which you did not discuss statements or the events that happened in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes. In my summer vacation, I think I had met him once or twice every week since he arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would go on during those meetings?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: It was quite strict. When we had a social meeting, we never discussed the case. So you always knew when we were discussing the case or when we just were socialising, drinking coffee, smoking, walking on the beach, whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you describe, just briefly, what you saw as his emotional and psychological condition during the time that he has been here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: He didn't like the Netherlands at all. I think many times he wanted to go back to Serbia or Bosnia. He didn't speak the language, he was nervous for the future, and he felt or meant that he had to wait too long to testify. So it was always a problem to deal with him. He could be in a bad mood one day and an excellent mood the next day. You never knew which mood he was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the sense that it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Paterson, could we learn from the witness how long he stayed in The Hague? Mr. Agnes, how long did he stay in The Hague before testifying in court?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: He arrived the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has he been here in The Hague since then?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout that time, was the witness in contact with Mr. Agnes?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I was in contact with him every week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a sense of how it affected him to have to talk about these events that had happened to him, both in 1992 in Bosanski Samac and the recent events he was describing?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: He didn't like to talk about it at all. It was hard for him. I could see he became nervous when we started talking about the case, maybe more about the camp period in Bosanski Samac, but also nervous when we discussed this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Paterson, if I understand well, Mr. Agnes has been here since the 19th of May, which is a long period of time now, a little over four months perhaps. Was this a period required by Mr. Agnes himself, for reasons of security, or did he stay here for so long because that was required of him by your office?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Would you like me to answer that question, Your Honour, or would you like me to ask Mr. Soldal that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You answer, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Agnes was brought here to The Hague for the sole purpose of testifying in this proceeding. He has been here since the 19th of May ready to testify in this proceeding and has simply been waiting for the hearing to be scheduled, and he has been kept here during that time for his own safety and security. Once the hearing concludes, he will be relocated to another location that we will obviously keep confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Paterson, he was kept here for reasons of his own security, waiting to testify; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: If I can just have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination from any of the concerned parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRASHICH
utterances.text: Not on behalf of Mr. Todorovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same on behalf of Mr. Tadic, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None on behalf of Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just so the Trial Chamber is clear as to my position, I will ask this witness a few questions now, but I would ask that he be returned for further cross-examination should we hear any more from Mr. Agnes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examined by Mr. Haynes:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly this, Mr. Soldal: During the course of your investigation into these matters, did you ever look into the question of whether Mr. Agnes had criminal convictions in any of the countries of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: We know about this incident with the girl, and we haven't checked him otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you made no check as to whether he has criminal convictions in Bosnia, Republika Srpska, or Serbia.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: We usually don't do that with witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than what he says about it, have you investigated the shooting of the girl in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No, we haven't investigated that, and I don't think that that's part of the OTP's jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, why not?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: It's as he explained it. There was no reason to think it was a war crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. It was as he explained it, and you took that at face value, did you?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No. It was also information about that incident from other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have information from other sources?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I know about that before. I talked to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether he faced any criminal charges in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I know there were some proceedings in the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the charges?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were charges, but you don't know what they were.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the girl died or not?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Only the information I have from the witness. He told me that he was told she died, but later on, somebody had told him that maybe she hadn't died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you haven't really looked into it at all, have you?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's quite possible, isn't it, that he was charged with murder?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that he escaped custody for that offence by the use of bribery of a public official.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: He told me that his father had -- uncle had paid somebody to get him released from the prison, and he had to stay in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's possible he could be a fugitive from a charge of murder.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I have no information to answer that, but it's a little bit strange that he went to be arrested in Serbia if he was wanted by the authorities in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Would you answer the question? Is it possible that he's a fugitive from a charge of murder?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on a bit now to the end of June. At the end of June, Mr. Avramovic and Mr. Simic filed documents setting out the nature of their defence to these charges. Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: End of June? I think so. I didn't see the latest one, but the end of June, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the contents of those documents discussed with Mr. Agnes?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not at all?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not in one of the conversations you had with him when you told him it was important he should tell everything?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more thing. You took his first statement over the course of two days, I think, on the 5th and 6th of May, at Camp McGovern.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes and no. We continued in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You continued the first statement in Sarajevo, did you?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When? On the 10th of May? I may have said June earlier on. I'm very sorry. I meant May, if I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes, I continued -- it was signed the 10th, and he was interviewed in the period between the 6th and the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first statement that we have is the product of how many days' interviewing?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I think four, because he wasn't interviewed every day. He was very tired, and we did this through phone calls and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first day, according to your declaration, you interviewed him for five hours.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes, and stayed in the camp with him for five hours, so it's difficult to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the second, for four and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was further interviewing on the subsequent two days; is that what you're now saying?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: We -- I interviewed him in the camp, I got the whole story in the camp, and then we stayed together in -- yes, until the 12th of May, and in the period between the 7th and the 10th, we were working on some details, especially dates. He had problems with dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The method of your interview, was it by you asking him questions and then recording the answers where they were relevant?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes, I was asking him questions, yes, but he was also speaking freely for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So it's a combination of voluntary disclosure by him coupled with questions from you and answers from him.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of those four days, did you ask him whether he had met Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume, from the contents of that statement, he said no.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you interviewed him again in The Hague on the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the method of interview the same?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No, because then it was a few details I wanted, so I asked him questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You asked him questions?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him about his contact with Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No, I don't think I asked that question during that interview, but I can't be 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't be 100 per cent sure. Do you have any notes of the interview?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you asked him how many times he spoke to him on the phone, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You asked him whether he had ever met him?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I could have asked him, but I don't think so, because then I hadn't any reason to believe that he had met Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The third interview, that's the 25th of May interview, can you give us some idea how long that took?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Normally, he met me around 1.30, so it could have taken three, four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 7th of June, you interviewed him again in The Hague, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over what length of time?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again on the 7th of June, you asked him whether he had ever met Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The 7th of June statement, he told me that he met Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How many times?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll help you. April 1999. Then on the 20th of July, you interviewed him for a fifth time in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again over a number of hours?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes. Then we interviewed him the 20 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I haven't come to that yet. I'm sorry, I have. The 20th of July, you interviewed him a fifth time?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The length of time?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Four hours or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four hours?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: And a readback the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you asked him about meeting Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: It wasn't me that asked him; it was he that told me or let me interview him about the story he told me some days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Can we take it that there was no perceptible difference in his demeanour between the interview taking place in May, the interview taking place on the 25th of May, the interview taking place on the 7th of June, and the interview taking place on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I mean did he look and behave much the same on the occasions of all of these interviews?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: More or less, he looked and behaved the same, but of course he knew me much better in late June than in the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think he was telling you the truth between the 6th and the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think he was telling you the truth on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The 25th of May, yes, because then I didn't ask a question about other things than some details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: The 7th of June, he told me immediately after he signed that there were more, so of course then I know that it wasn't the truth, the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your belief that the 20th of July is the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we just correct the record, that that statement was not taken on the 20th of July; it was taken on the 20th of June, if we could just correct the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you ought to look at your own documents. You've corrected that in a document that you filed with the Chamber, because we raised the question of the dates on that statement. Your own document confirms it's the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: I'll let Mr. Soldal explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your belief, is it, that the 20th of July is the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: You're asking me the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I think that's almost the whole truth. There can be more details that he means is not important for the case, but I think it's the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me see if you agree with this as a summary of what he told you on the 20th of July: A handful of meetings with Mr. Simic and the lawyers?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say to you at any stage that he had met them up to ten times a month?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: That he met the lawyers or Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either that he had meetings with the lawyers or Mr. Simic up to ten times a month. Did he ever say that?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Not that I remember, but he described -- tried to describe every meeting and placed them on a time line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us as to how we can tell when he's telling the truth and when he isn't?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: I can help you how? Sorry, can you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You thought he was telling the truth in May, but he wasn't?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything about his demeanour in May that indicated to you he was lying?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No, but I didn't know him well then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him a lot better by the end of May, didn't you? Was there anything about his demeanour on the 25th of May, when you spent several hours with him, that indicated to you that he was lying?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No, because, as I already have told, I only asked him some details. You can see there are not such big differences between the statement signed the 10th and the statement signed the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go straight to the 20th of July, then. If it be his account now that there were many, many, many more meetings than he described to you, was there anything about his demeanour on the 20th of July that indicated to you that he was lying?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it wasn't the truth on the 20th of July, you, who knows him better than anybody in this courtroom, couldn't tell?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Of course, I can't tell when people are telling the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Soldal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Paterson:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Soldal, I want to direct your attention to this fourth statement that was taken on the 7th of June. Do you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement, Mr. Agnes made some reference to going to a meeting in Bosanski Samac in April of this year. Do you recall that part of the statement?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you since been able to determine whether or not that date at the beginning of April this year is, in fact, correct, or was that somehow a misunderstanding between you and Mr. Agnes?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: When I had finished the statement, I put it into an analyst's notebook, this analyst programme we use at the OTP, and made a time line and showed it to him; and he, when he read the time line, he said, "This meeting is wrong because it was before the air strike."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you talked with him about it subsequently, he corrected himself and --

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- said that meeting did not happen in April; is that right? Mr. Soldal, Mr. Haynes has just asked you whether or not you believed Mr. Agnes, whether you thought he was telling you the truth. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court what it is that you rely on in making your assessment that Mr. Agnes has been telling you the truth, other than the fact of his demeanour, as Mr. Haynes was asking you? What are the points that, to you, convince you that Mr. Agnes is telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: TORE SOLDAL
utterances.text: First of all, he has never asked me for anything. He has never been -- never asked me to take him out of the country, he never asked me for money, for a job, so I can't understand why he should lie. For me, there is no reason for that. Secondly, when you read a statement, you can see that, yes, he has lied, but it was always a reason. He wanted to protect family, friends, and so on. He lied when he said that he hadn't met Milan Simic. He lied about how he came to Bosanski Samac this evening before the war started. The next statement where he told -- or the fourth statement where he told he had met Milan Simic only once, he told me immediately after he had signed the statement that he had much more information, but he wouldn't tell it because it was too dangerous for people living in Samac. So in some ways, I can understand why he gave the story this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Soldal, thanks for your testimony. You're released.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Those are then all the witnesses we have to adduce at this time. You indicated you would take the adjournment when we indicated that we had this further witness. Those are our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ryneveld. As I indicated before, at the commencement of tomorrow's session at 2.30, we will hear from the head of the Victims and Witnesses Unit. The Registrar is required to pass on that information to the Victims and Witnesses Unit. We take the adjournment now until 2.30 tomorrow.
